incremental_scope: Native SQL PREPARE/EXECUTE accepted provenance, full pinned pg_dump compatibility, unchanged exact SQL bytes and unchanged conservative exclusions.

findings.assessment: The prior real pg_dump run reached 68 accepted queries and was correctly denied on PREPARE getColumnACLs(pg_catalog.oid) AS a static SELECT. Pinned PostgreSQL 16.15 primary source pg_dump.c:15373 establishes that query family. Other pinned static PREPARE sites exist for domains, types, functions and operators. Keeping complete native backups is preferable to dropping ACLs to evade the requirement.

The whole PREPARE source, including static body, and every EXECUTE source must each pass exact SQLean grammar admission. No percent-parameter substitution or SQL regeneration is introduced by Allow. Source bytes forwarded to PostgreSQL remain unchanged.

Unquoted simple ASCII names of at most 63 bytes and ASCII-only lowercase normalization avoid quoted/Unicode/long-name ambiguity. Protocol names remain exact; a shared connection-local provenance namespace supports cross-protocol operations without conflating SQL lexical normalization with protocol strings.

EXECUTE needs a previously admitted target plus its own admitted exact source; connection boundaries and existing object/metadata caps remain mandatory. A Bind portal retains its immutable accepted payload across replacement. Optimistic admission must never be presented as PostgreSQL execution success or exact server-object correspondence after an error.

Sole top-level native statements only; reject nested/multi combinations and apply all existing opaque-production, unsafe set_config, lexer-mode and resource restrictions to PREPARE bodies and EXECUTE expressions. Arbitrary function-effect analysis is explicitly not claimed.

SQL DEALLOCATE, two-phase prepared transactions, DO/function/procedure dynamic bodies, and fast-path calls remain rejected. Managed psycopg automatic preparation is disabled while ordinary extended parameter binding remains supported.

implementation_acceptance_obligations: Real full pg_dump/pg_restore with ACLs through canonical proxy endpoints; distinct client counter evidence and unchanged backup content.
Native PREPARE/EXECUTE success; unknown/cross-connection target rejection; both SQL-to-protocol Bind and protocol-Parse-to-SQL EXECUTE.
Quoted, Unicode, overlong and ambiguous names reject; uppercase ASCII names normalize only for lookup, never mutate SQL source.
Nested EXPLAIN EXECUTE, CREATE AS EXECUTE, multi-statement combinations, unsafe mode functions inside prepared bodies and EXECUTE arguments reject before forwarding.
Retain original rev3 failed backup evidence and original strict policy snapshot; do not reinterpret prior failure as a pass.
Re-run fresh/idempotent/partial/drift migration and real restore/revocation tests after the approved proxy implementation.
implementation_plan_unchanged: My production ownership remains canonical connection enforcement, bootstrap, explicit migration/catalog validation and real recovery routing. All source/SQL/test mutations are paused until final rev4 proof/council release.
formal_limit: Await exact final spec hash and additional Lean obligations. This is a design review, not an implementation approval or proof of PostgreSQL semantics.

new_claim_review.SQ17: A reachable native EXECUTE carries its own admitted request and a known admitted target statement.
new_claim_review.SQ18: Unknown native target cannot execute in the model.
new_claim_review.SQ19: Native PREPARE can feed the shared Bind/portal path while preserving admitted request/report provenance.
new_claim_review.SQ20: Successful cache lookup is pure and cannot create a prepared statement.
new_claim_review.SQ21_SQ22: Explicit nonempty native PREPARE and EXECUTE witnesses make the new policy non-vacuous.

body_span_trust_boundary: Read NativePrepare/bodyPart and their Lean documentation. bodyPart proves only a nonempty substring decomposition of the whole accepted source; correct SQL statement classification, actual body-span identification and ASCII name correspondence remain trusted adapter obligations. The review does not infer a verified parser AST/body mapping or PostgreSQL execution semantics from these theorems.
final_conclusion: Approve exact revision 4 design with no remaining design blockers. Runtime protocol, body/name extraction, native full backup, migration and restore/revocation checks remain implementation acceptance obligations. Production remains paused until the parent announces formal/council release.
